newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INTER MAKE URGENT APPEAL AGAINST INCE BAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER MAKE URGENT APPEAL AGAINST INCE BAN.

text.p: Italian league leaders Inter said on Wednesday they had filed an urgent appeal against a two match ban given to England midfielder Paul Ince after he was controversially sent off in a weekend match.

Ince was shown the red card after Piacenza's Giampietro Piovani, waiting for a corner to be taken, collapsed theatrically in the goalmouth clutching his head as if he had been hit by the Englishman in an off the ball foul.

Television replays showed clearly that Ince had merely tweaked the Italian's ear. Newspapers said that Ince, who is black, had also been provoked by a racist taunt that Piovani later admitted making in the heat of the moment.
The serie A sporting judge confirmed the ban was for hitting an opponent "at ear level".
Piovani, who was sent off in the closing seconds for elbowing an opponent, was also banned for two matches.
Inter are due to play European Cup holders Juventus on Sunday and against Parma the following weekend.
French international Christian Karembeu and Germany's Euro 96 star forward Oliver Bierhoff were also given two match bans after being sent off at the weekend.
Sampdoria's Karembeu was sent off in the second half of his team's 2-1 defeat against Bologna on Sunday for hitting opponent Igor Shalimov after being fouled by the Russian.
Bierhoff was sent off for a particularly bad foul in Udinese's 1-1 draw at Napoli on Sunday. The German had earlier scored his team's equaliser.
